raw.title: Senior Product Marketing Manager, Enterprise Products
raw.description:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Senior Product Marketing Manager, Enterprise Products to shape how we position, launch, and scale our enterprise products like Vibe and Studio.

This is a high-impact role at the intersection of product, technology, and go-to-market strategy. You’ll translate complex product capabilities into clear, differentiated value propositions that resonate with enterprise decision-makers, technical buyers, and practitioners. You’ll define how we take our products to market, build repeatable messaging and enablement frameworks, and equip our commercial teams to articulate why Mistral is the right partner for organisations adopting AI at scale.

Working closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, Solutions, Developer Relations, and Communications, you’ll influence both how our products evolve and how we bring them to market. You’ll help establish the foundations for scaling our enterprise platform business in a rapidly evolving and highly competitive AI landscape.

What you will do

Product positioning and messaging

  • Own positioning and messaging for Mistral’s enterprise products, translating technical capabilities into differentiated value propositions for enterprise customers.

  • Develop compelling narratives that connect platform functionality to business outcomes, technical requirements, and customer priorities.

  • Tailor messaging to different audiences, from CIOs and technology leaders to developers, AI engineers, and business stakeholders.

  • Define our competitive positioning against proprietary AI platforms, hyperscalers, and emerging alternatives, articulating the value of Mistral’s open-weight models, flexibility, and deployment options.

  • Build a consistent messaging architecture across products, use cases, customer segments, and go-to-market channels.

Go-to-market strategy and product launches

  • Lead go-to-market strategy for new enterprise platform capabilities, from launch planning and audience definition to positioning, activation, and post-launch optimisation.

  • Partner with Product and Engineering to understand the roadmap, identify market opportunities, and translate product developments into compelling customer propositions.

  • Identify high-value enterprise use cases and customer segments, developing repeatable GTM plays that support adoption and commercial growth.

  • Establish clear launch frameworks, working cross-functionally to align Product, Sales, Solutions, Marketing, Communications, and Developer Relations around priorities and execution.

  • Measure launch effectiveness and product adoption, using customer feedback and performance data to refine positioning and GTM strategy.

Sales and field enablement

  • Equip Sales and Solutions teams with the messaging, assets, and commercial narratives they need to position Mistral’s enterprise platforms effectively.

  • Develop scalable enablement materials, including use-case playbooks, competitive battlecards, customer presentations, product demos, and objection-handling guides.

  • Translate customer challenges and technical requirements into compelling business cases that support enterprise evaluation and purchasing decisions.

  • Partner with field teams to identify recurring customer objections, competitive dynamics, and barriers to adoption, feeding these insights back into product and marketing strategy.

  • Build repeatable frameworks that help commercial teams communicate platform value consistently across industries, markets, and buyer personas.

Content and customer storytelling

  • Develop a content strategy that brings Mistral’s enterprise platform capabilities to life through product narratives, technical explainers, demonstrations, customer stories, and thought leadership.

  • Work with Content, Communications, Developer Relations, and Solutions teams to create credible, technically grounded content that resonates with enterprise buyers and practitioners.

  • Turn customer implementations and emerging use cases into compelling stories that demonstrate measurable business value.

  • Support integrated campaigns and demand generation initiatives with clear messaging, audience insights, and content tailored to the enterprise buying journey.

  • Ensure our content connects technical differentiation to the practical realities of deploying and scaling AI in enterprise environments.

Market intelligence and customer insights

  • Develop a strong understanding of enterprise AI adoption, platform buying behaviour, competitive offerings, and emerging customer needs.

  • Gather insights from customers, prospects, Sales, Solutions, and partners to identify unmet needs, adoption barriers, and opportunities for differentiation.

  • Build a clear view of the competitive landscape, translating market intelligence into actionable recommendations for product positioning, roadmap priorities, and GTM investments.

  • Identify emerging enterprise AI use cases and market segments where Mistral can establish a differentiated position.

  • Track the impact of positioning and GTM initiatives through relevant measures, including product adoption, pipeline influence, sales enablement effectiveness, and launch performance.

What we're looking for

  • Deep experience in product marketing, ideally within enterprise software, AI platforms, cloud infrastructure, developer tools, or other technically complex products.

  • A proven track record of developing differentiated product positioning and messaging that translates technical capabilities into clear customer and business value.

  • Experience leading product launches and building go-to-market strategies for enterprise technology products, from early positioning through adoption and commercial scale.

  • Strong understanding of enterprise buying journeys, including technical evaluation, stakeholder alignment, procurement considerations, and the challenges of deploying new technologies at scale.

  • Ability to engage credibly with technical audiences while communicating effectively with executive and business stakeholders.

  • Experience partnering closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, Solutions, and other cross-functional teams to drive alignment and execution.

  • A commercial mindset, with the ability to connect product marketing initiatives to adoption, pipeline development, deal progression, and revenue growth.

  • Strong competitive and market intelligence skills, with the ability to turn customer and market insights into actionable GTM strategies.

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with a talent for simplifying complex concepts into clear, compelling narratives.

  • A hands-on, proactive approach and the ability to operate independently, navigate ambiguity, and build repeatable processes in a fast-moving environment.

Nice to have

  • Experience marketing AI platforms, model platforms, cloud infrastructure, or enterprise developer tools.

  • Familiarity with LLMs, open-weight models, AI deployment architectures, and the practical challenges organisations face when moving AI from experimentation into production.

  • Experience marketing products to both technical practitioners and enterprise decision-makers.

  • Understanding of enterprise AI requirements, including security, governance, privacy, scalability, and deployment flexibility.

  • Experience working in a high-growth technology company where product positioning, GTM strategy, and operating models are still evolving.

Why join Mistral?

At Mistral, you’ll help shape how organisations adopt and scale AI through products that give them greater choice and control over their technology. You’ll work alongside world-class researchers, engineers, product leaders, and commercial teams to bring ambitious ideas to market.

This is an opportunity to have a meaningful impact on our enterprise strategy, build the foundations for repeatable product marketing at scale, and help define how one of Europe’s leading AI companies competes in a global market.

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page.

What You'll Deliver in the First 6-12 Months

• Consulting engagement, tracked: how many one-to-ones and team sessions helped others learn or unblock. (Tech-enabled, human-centred)

• At least two high-value workflows mapped and redesigned with the teams that own them, with a before-and-after in hours or money agreed with the owner. (Chase 10X, not 10%)

• AI Acceleration's own intake and tracking running with less manual coordination, owned end to end within a defined remit.

Minimum Qualifications

• One to three examples of taking a business problem, listening to it, and building and deploying a solution, with at least one owned end to end on moderate complexity and limited guidance. Internships, early roles and strong projects count.

• Process mapping, or visible willingness to learn it quickly. A short course is available.

• Working familiarity with applied AI: large language models, context, retrieval, agents, connectors and evaluation.

• A bias toward adoption: goes back, watches the team work with it, and helps work out what is not landing.

Preferred Qualifications

• A background in GTM engineering, solutions consulting or AI operations.

• Empathy and a supportive instinct: can teach non-engineers and stay with a team through a build.

• An interest in systems: sees AI Acceleration as itself a workflow worth improving.

raw.title: Area Medical Leads, North and South
raw.description:
Mission

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear.

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.

Role Purpose

You own the clinical bar across the Neko clinics in the North (currently Birmingham and Manchester) or South (currently London) regions of the UK.

That means every consultation in your area meets the same threshold of safety, quality, and member experience across your region. It means the clinical teams working with you are developing, not just performing. It means clinical issues are being seen and addressed before they show up in audits or member complaints. And it means the quality metrics for your region are known, owned and moving in the right direction. And it means clinical judgment shows up at the table when operational decisions are being made.

You'll partner closely with the UK Medical Director, who holds final clinical authority for the UK market, and operate in true dyad partnership with the Area Clinic Manager for your region who owns the operational side. The clinical health of the region is yours.

What You'll Deliver in the First 6–12 Months

  • Hold the clinical standard across every site in your area

  • Manage and develop the clinicians in your region: performance conversations, development plans, coaching, and the honest feedback that turns good clinicians into great ones.

  • Ensure lead clinicians in your market(s) are performing excellently and that the clinical teams have the appropriate clinical escalation pathways in place.

  • Support clinical hiring for your area against defined criteria, and partner with the Training and Education team to close training gaps as they emerge.

  • Own the review and closure of clinical incidents and near-misses in your area, making sure learnings are actually applied, not just documented.

  • Own the quality metrics for your region: accountable for performance against Neko's medical quality goals at area level, including scan quality (perfect scan score), member follow-up quality and timeliness (perfect follow-up score and follow-up SLAs), clinical safety (Northstar Clinical Safety score) and clinician summary quality and timeliness. Review the data with your Area Clinic Manager each week and month, trace variation to root cause by site and clinician, set improvement actions, and report progress and risks to the UK Medical Director.

  • Operate in true dyad partnership with the Area Clinic Manager: co-owning quality, member experience, and business goals, attending and contributing to Weekly and Monthly Business Reviews, and bringing clinical input into operational decisions before they're made.

  • Round your sites regularly to observe, support, and listen, surfacing what's working so it can spread, and what isn't so it can be addressed.

  • Build and maintain trusted relationships with the GPs, NHS trusts and private specialist clinicians who receive Neko referrals, monitoring referral quality and addressing breakdowns quickly.

  • Know the UK regulatory landscape: CQC registration and inspection standards, GMC/NMC professional standards and revalidation, NHS and GP referral pathways and obligations, and UK-specific clinical rules, and flag emerging risks before they become problems.

  • Lead or participate in clinical pilots as required - defining success, capturing learnings, and documenting outcomes so the rest of the company can learn from your region.

What We're Hiring For

  • Holds the Bar at Scale. You're the kind of clinical leader who can make sure every consultation feels the same regardless of site or clinician, not by micromanaging, but by setting a clear standard, coaching to it, and noticing when it drifts. You're rigorous without being rigid.

  • Develops the Clinicians You Lead. You take clinician development seriously. You give honest feedback even when it's uncomfortable. You spot what someone needs before they ask. You know the difference between a clinician who needs coaching and one who needs to leave, and you don't avoid either conversation.

  • The Dyad That Actually Works. You bring clinical judgment into operational decisions before they're made and you stay constructive when clinical standards and operational targets pull in different directions. When you escalate, it's because something genuinely needs leadership attention, not because you've stopped trying to resolve it locally.

  • Reads the Pattern, Not Just the Report. You don't just review the data. You see what it's telling you. You round your sites and notice things that don't show up in dashboards. When you spot a pattern you trace it to the root cause and you make sure the right people hear about it.

  • Trusted Outside the Walls. The referral network, the regulators, the specialist clinicians who receive Neko members: these relationships sit with you. You represent Neko credibly because you're a credible clinician yourself. People in the local medical community know your name, and when you flag something, they take it seriously.

Minimum Requirements

  • Full GMC registration with a license to practice, in good standing and with a current revalidation, and right to work in the UK.

  • On the GMC GP Register with qualification (CCT or equivalent) in General Practice.

  • 4+ years of medical leadership experience in the UK health system (NHS and/or private sector), including direct management of clinicians.

  • Demonstrated experience holding clinical standards across multiple sites or a large clinical team.

Preferred

  • Experience in preventive care, tech enabled healthcare or longitudinal care models.

  • Experience operating in a clinical-operational dyad structure.

  • Experience leading clinical pilots or scaling new clinical workflows across multiple sites.

Interviews are ongoing, so don’t hesitate to send in your application today!

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.

Role Purpose

This role exists to keep clinics staffed to target coverage. The Workforce Management Specialist owns bi-weekly and monthly rota creation, maintains accurate schedules in the workforce management system, and produces the staffing reports that let clinic and market leadership make fast, informed decisions. The role sits within the Operations Planning function and partners directly with clinic leads on coverage, staffing, and labour metrics.

 

What You'll Deliver in the First 6-12 Months

  • Own accurate, on-time bi-weekly/monthly rota publication for all assigned Swedish clinics, with late changes, swaps, and backfills handled without service disruption.

  • Establish daily tracking of open shifts and coverage gaps across assigned clinics, with escalation to bank pools and agency partners triggered before gaps affect throughput.

  • Administer Quinyx (locations, roles, templates, policies, leave rules) for assigned clinics and configure at least one automation that measurably reduces manual admin time (Tech-enabled, human-centred).

  • Deliver a reliable weekly staffing pack (coverage %, overtime, additional hours, tardiness, utilisation, variance vs plan) that clinic and market leadership use to make staffing decisions.

  • Reduce payroll queries and adjustments through cleaner timesheet reconciliation and consistent HRIS-to-payroll data flow.

 

Minimum Qualifications

  • Previous experience in strategic workforce planning (Quinyx is preferable but other systems are accepted)

  • Comfortable in Excel: filters, lookups, pivot basics, conditional formatting; able to analyse CSVs and spot anomalies

  • Demonstrated ownership of detail-heavy, deadline-driven admin work (the "last mile" that keeps a rota accurate)

  • Demonstrated ability to build recurring reporting/dashboards (Tableau, Power BI, or advanced Excel) covering variance-to-plan, utilization, or forecast accuracy

  • Experience improving data integrity or process efficiency in a workforce data pipeline

raw.title: Director Accounting & Finance - FTC
raw.description:
Who We Are:
At Omaze, we give our community in the UK and Germany the chance to win luxury homes and other life-changing prizes — all while raising money for the causes they love.

Thanks to our Omaze Community, we’ve raised over £150 million for UK charities in just five years. That’s millions helping organisations like Age UK, the RSPCA, British Heart Foundation and Great Ormond Street Hospital Charity deliver life-saving work.

And the best part? We’re only just getting started. Omaze is building a business and culture committed to growth and creating significant social impact on a global scale.

🔑 About The Job

We’re looking for an experienced, hands-on accounting and finance leader to provide maternity cover of 14 months during a period of continued business development and finance transformation.

This is a broad role combining financial reporting, month-end delivery, cash and debt-facility reporting, corporate governance support and finance-systems ownership. You’ll work closely with the CFO, Finance and Accounting colleagues, business leaders and external advisers to maintain reliable reporting, effective controls and continuity across key workstreams.

You’ll be equally comfortable reviewing accounting entries, explaining budget variances, coordinating an audit and resolving a NetSuite reporting or access issue. Success will mean keeping essential processes running smoothly while progressing agreed improvements and making risks, decisions and dependencies visible.


🥇 What success looks like

  • Month-end close, consolidated reporting and board-reporting inputs are delivered accurately and on time.

  • Lender reporting and compliance requirements are met, with clear oversight of deadlines and dependencies.

  • Budget holders receive useful analysis and timely support.

  • Audit and adviser workstreams progress with clear ownership and well-organised evidence.

  • Finance systems remain reliable, and agreed implementation and reporting improvements continue.

  • Responsibilities, decisions and outstanding matters are documented to support a smooth handover back.

🔧 What You’ll Be Doing

Audit, governance, tax and technical accounting

  • Coordinate audit delivery, acting as a central contact for auditors and internal stakeholders and tracking evidence requests, issues and deadlines.

  • Draft consolidated and entity level financial statements along with relevant footnote disclosures under IFRS and US GAAP.

  • Initiate implementation of IFRA 18 and ASU 2024-03.

  • Support corporate governance processes and associated financial documentation and reporting.

  • Support the CFO with Senior Accounting Officer (SAO) and Corporate Criminal Offence (CCO) workstreams, including documentation, information gathering and follow-through on agreed actions.

  • Coordinate accounting advisory workstreams, ensuring clear briefs, ownership, timely responses and resolution of outstanding matters.

  • Ad hoc technical accounting assessments, documenting agreed conclusions and supporting implementation.

Financial accounting, close and consolidated reporting

  • Deliver assigned month-end close activities, including intercompany eliminations, and coordinate with entity accounting teams.

  • Prepare and coordinate consolidated monthly financial reporting under US GAAP and IFRS, ensuring completeness, consistency and clear explanations of significant movements.

  • Review assigned journals, reconciliations and intercompany activity, resolving issues with the relevant preparers and reviewers.

  • Maintain close timetables, support the resolution of blockers and ensure appropriate documentation and review evidence.

  • Support the preparation and validation of financial actuals and analysis for board reporting.

Equity administration and insurance

  • Administer Carta, including reporting, supporting bookkeeping, maintaining records and coordinating approved changes with relevant stakeholders.

  • Coordinate corporate, office and other insurance matters, working with brokers, Legal and business owners on renewals, coverage questions, policy changes and emerging requirements.

  • Maintain clear records of outstanding actions, approvals and responsibilities across both workstreams.

Finance systems and reporting

  • Act as the day-to-day Netsuite administrator, covering month-end requirements, ongoing maintenance, user access, configuration and issue resolution.

  • Facilitate work with external Netsuite support partners, prioritising requests and coordinating delivery, testing and implementation.

  • Develop and maintain Netsuite reporting for Finance, including reports and saved searches that improve visibility and reduce manual work.

  • Administer and maintain Netsuite Account Reconciliation system, including period roll-forwards, assignments and troubleshooting.

Cash, treasury and loan facility reporting

  • Coordinate monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting, certificates, utilisation requests and other required submissions, including event-triggered reporting.

  • Maintain a clear compliance calendar and work with the CFO, Legal and Accounting teams to ensure timely, accurate reporting and escalation.

🤩 About You

Essential experience and skills

  • A recognised accounting qualification ACA, ACCA, CPA or equivalent.

  • Experience drafting consolidated and entity-level financial statements under both IFRS and US GAAP.

  • Strong experience across financial accounting, consolidated reporting and month-end close in a multi-national environment.

  • Strong hands-on NetSuite experience, including administration, reporting and working with external support partners.

  • Experience coordinating external audits and managing relationships with professional advisers.

  • Confidence managing cash reporting, debt-facility reporting and compliance deadlines.

  • Sound technical accounting judgement, with the ability to identify when specialist advice or escalation is needed.

  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to prioritise competing operational and project demands and supporting Accounting and Finance team members.

  • Clear communication and the confidence to challenge constructively, explain complex issues and drive actions to completion.

Desirable experience

  • UK and US accounting and reporting requirements, including US GAAP and IFRS.

  • NSAR and NSPB administration or implementation.

  • Carta and equity-related accounting or administration.

  • Senior Accounting Officer support (familiarity with Criminal Finance Act), insurance coordination or corporate governance support.

  • Subscription, e-commerce or other high-volume transaction businesses.

🙌 What’s In It For You

  • 25 days annual leave PLUS Bank Holidays

  • Private medical and dental insurance

  • 9% employer pension contributions, when you contribute at least 2%

  • A generous personal learning and development budget each year to use on training courses, conferences and professional memberships

  • Enhanced family leave policies

  • Life assurance of 4x your salary

DEI Statement

We actively seek out diversity of thought and experience to drive innovation. We welcome all backgrounds, identities, and perspectives and work hard to ensure that every Omaze employee can bring their authentic self to work at all times.

raw.title: Strategic Account Manager
raw.description:
Our Mission:

Omnea is the agentic operating system for procurement.

Procurement touches every pound a business spends, yet requests still stall for weeks and approvals get lost in inboxes. Our AI-first platform changes that: our agents capture requests, route approvals, onboard suppliers, flag risk and track every renewal, while anyone in the business can ask a question and get an answer grounded in their own company’s data. Buying becomes painless for everyone, procurement gets a seat at the table, and our customers have saved more than 100,000 hours of manual work so far.

Companies like Spotify, PayPal, T. Rowe Price, JustEat, Adyen and S&P Global run procurement on Omnea. We’re backed by $75M from Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners and Accel, and we’ve been named the UK’s number one startup in the Startups 100, ranked 11th on Sifted’s 2026 list of Europe’s fastest-growing companies, and recognised as one of Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies.

Talent density matters more to us than almost anything else. We keep the bar high in every team, so everyone here has real ownership and real impact. Our team is full of former founders and operators who’ve scaled unicorns, and we’re looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers alongside them.

Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here.

The Role

As Omnea's Account Manager, you own the relationship with our customers across their entire lifecycle, working with some of our largest and most strategic accounts. Your job is to make sure customers get real, measurable value from Omnea from day one, and to turn that value into renewals, expansion, and upsell.

Omnea's product is sticky: it's a business transformation, not a point tool, so once a customer is live, expansion tends to follow. Your focus skews heavily toward that expansion motion, not just keeping accounts renewed.

You'll build deep, long-term relationships with your champions and become a trusted advisor to stakeholders at every level, from procurement managers up to CFOs. You'll be the internal voice of the customer, working closely with both technical and commercial teams to keep Omnea customer-centric at its core.

This is an early hire on the customer team, working directly with Abs, Ben, and Rebe to build the function from the ground up. There's no fixed playbook yet: you'll help write it.

What You'll Do

  • Own a revenue number: You'll carry an NRR quota covering both expansion and retention across your enterprise book. That means proactively identifying upsell opportunities, running commercial conversations at exec level, and owning the renewal process end-to-end.

  • Build relationships that go all the way to the top: Your relationships will run from procurement managers to CFOs. You'll multi-thread across each account, building genuine trust across multiple stakeholders, and you'll be the person customers call when something goes wrong or when they're thinking about what's next.

  • Build the playbook from scratch: There's no fully built playbook yet - you'll help shape it. You'll work alongside an exceptional implementation team, product experts, and leadership that have scaled world-class companies to define the commercial rhythms, norms, and processes to set the standard as the function grows.

  • Shape what Omnea builds next: You're the closest person to what our customers will and won't pay for. You'll feed that signal directly to Product and Revenue leadership, surfacing what's blocking adoption, what's driving expansion, and where we should be investing.

What's Different About This Role

  • This isn't a traditional post-sale account management role. Omnea's product is a business transformation, not a point tool, so most of your quota comes from expansion, not just renewal.

  • We're not looking for a narrow "Account Manager" background. We want people from GTM roles broadly or from customer-facing roles with heavy commercial/GTM crossover.

  • There's no fully built playbook. You'll define the commercial rhythms and processes as you go, working directly with Abs, Ben, and Rebe.

  • You'll be as close to the product roadmap as anyone outside Product itself: what you hear from customers directly shapes what gets built next.

About You

We don't expect you to know exactly how to do all of this when you join. We're looking for someone with the right attitude and skillset to take this on.

TL;DR: you're commercially sharp, and you instinctively know how to navigate complex organisations. You might come from a GTM role (sales, customer success, partnerships) or a customer-facing role with heavy GTM crossover. What matters is that you've worked in real enterprise environments, managed senior stakeholders with high expectations, and have a track record of getting things done.

  • 4-8 years of experience in a top-tier, fast-paced environment: a startup, scale-up, VC, consulting, banking, or something you built yourself

    • If you've been in a commercial role, you've worked six-figure ARR+ accounts, navigated multi-stakeholder buying committees, and built genuine executive relationships

  • You build rapport, influence people, and drive change, whether with a distinguished exec or a junior operator. You have the gravitas to engage senior leadership, ideally up to CFOs, Legal, or Procurement

  • You're comfortable in ambiguity. You don't need a fully built playbook: you'll build it as you go and improve it as you learn. You're organised enough to manage a complex book of business without dropping anything, and confident enough to push back on customers when they're wrong

  • You're ambitious, competitive, and care about doing excellent work, with a track record of high performance in whatever you've turned your hand to: sales, academia, sport, or something of your own. You take ownership seriously, and you'd rather work hard on something meaningful than coast on something safe

At Omnea, we embrace diversity. To build a product that's loved by everyone, we're best served by a team with all sorts of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't quite match the full job spec! And regardless of your race, religion, colour, gender, or anything else! If you think you could be a good fit for Omnea, please reach out.

A few things to note:

  • We offer competitive geo-localised benefits, and you can check out our UK Benefits Package here and our US Benefits Package here.

  • We work Tuesdays, Wednesdays & Thursdays in-person at our offices. At this early stage of our company life-cycle it's important to us that we get this together-time, and you can read more about why we believe this is a winning move here

  • We're commercial, ambitious and we don't pretend otherwise! We're actively seeking folks looking to make the most of a career-defining opportunity, with the hunger to be part of building something really impressive. You can see our values here and our Omnea Future Founder's fund here!

  • We sometimes use AI note-takers to help us transcribe interview notes, so we can be more present in your interview. If you'd like to opt out of us using automatic transcribers, please note this in the free text field in your application, otherwise we'll take your application as confirmation that you're happy for us to use notetakers (whether added to video calls or in the background).

We are proud to be recognised for both our culture and product, and we are just getting started. Join us as we grow!

Legal note: if you are viewing this posting outside of the Omnea careers' page, this may be an auto-generated advertisement and may lack the full range of advertised information - please click through to the posting at https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/omnea to view additional advertised information on this posting.
Additionally, where roles have hard-specified requirements (e.g. [x] days in office, unable to provide visas, etc), if in your application you provide deterministic check-box confirmation that you do not meet the hard-specified requirements, deterministic (not AI or subjective) automatic rejection criteria are in place.

raw.title: Head of Agency, EMEA - Ad Solutions
raw.description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. In support of that mission, the Ads Solutions team partners closely with advertisers, agencies and strategic partners to help businesses unlock value through AI-powered advertising solutions while maintaining strong standards for user trust, platform integrity and responsible innovation.

As OpenAI’s advertising business continues to scale globally, the Head of Agency, EMEA will play a critical role in developing strategic agency partnerships, accelerating advertiser adoption and shaping how agencies help their clients succeed with OpenAI. You will work closely with EMEA and global leadership to translate our advertising strategy into a clear plan for the region’s agency ecosystem.

About the Role

We are seeking an Head of Agency, EMEA - Ad Solutions to lead and scale OpenAI’s agency partnerships across Europe, the Middle East and Africa. You will own the regional agency strategy, building relationships with agency holding companies, their networks and leading independent agencies to drive sustainable revenue growth and advertiser success. This role is based in London and reports to the Head of Ads Solutions for EMEA.

This is a highly strategic and hands-on leadership role. You will engage senior agency executives, develop joint business plans and commercial partnerships, and work with country sales and customer success teams to turn regional agreements into meaningful local execution. You will help agencies build the knowledge, capabilities and confidence to incorporate OpenAI’s advertising solutions into their clients’ marketing strategies.

You will partner closely with Product, Engineering, Marketing, Operations and Policy teams to ensure agency and advertiser feedback informs product development and go-to-market decisions. Working alongside global agency teams, you will align international partnerships with the needs of EMEA markets and help establish scalable ways of working across the region.

The ideal candidate combines deep knowledge of the EMEA agency landscape with strong commercial judgement, executive influence and operational rigour. You are equally comfortable negotiating a strategic partnership, working with local teams to unlock client opportunities, and helping agency leaders understand the possibilities of AI-powered advertising.

In this role, you will:

  • Develop and execute OpenAI’s EMEA agency strategy, prioritising partnerships, markets and growth opportunities across agency holding companies, networks and independent agencies.

  • Own agency partnership revenue goals and business performance, working with country leaders to establish clear targets, accountabilities and execution plans.

  • Build and maintain executive-level relationships with agency leaders across management, investment, trading, strategy, planning, activation, data and measurement.

  • Develop joint business plans that connect agency priorities with advertiser outcomes, with clear commitments, milestones and measures of success.

  • Lead the development and negotiation of regional trading agreements and strategic commercial partnerships, working closely with Finance, Legal and regional leadership.

  • Translate regional and global agency agreements into local activation, coordinating with country sales and customer success teams on account plans, advertiser onboarding and growth.

  • Expand the number of agency clients advertising with OpenAI and deepen adoption across relevant products and use cases.

  • Partner with Marketing and customer-facing teams to deliver agency education, leadership engagement and enablement programmes that build lasting capability across planning and buying teams.

  • Establish a disciplined operating cadence for pipeline management, forecasting, partnership reviews and tracking delivery against commercial commitments.

  • Define clear ways of working across agency, direct advertiser, country and global account teams to coordinate customer engagement and support shared growth.

  • Bring agency and advertiser insights to Product, Engineering and leadership teams, helping identify opportunities to improve the customer experience, measurement and product adoption.

  • Provide strategic direction and coaching to colleagues working on agency partnerships across EMEA, building shared playbooks and consistently high standards of execution.

  • Represent OpenAI’s advertising offering in senior agency discussions and industry forums, maintaining a strong commitment to user trust and responsible innovation.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 15+ years of experience in the advertising industry, including significant experience in agency partnerships, digital advertising sales or senior agency leadership.

  • Have a proven track record of exceeding revenue targets and building strategic agency partnerships across multiple EMEA markets.

  • Bring deep knowledge of the EMEA agency ecosystem and established senior relationships across agency holding companies, networks and independent agencies.

  • Have experience developing and negotiating complex trading agreements, joint business plans and multi-market commercial partnerships, and translating them into measurable results.

  • Understand how agency investment decisions are made and can build relationships across executive leadership, trading, planning, activation, data and measurement teams.

  • Can articulate a compelling business case for a new advertising platform, connecting brand and performance objectives with relevant products and credible measurement.

  • Combine strong strategic thinking with a bias towards execution, operational excellence and personal accountability.

  • Are highly data-driven and comfortable using analytics to prioritise investment, assess partnership performance and identify opportunities for growth.

  • Have experience leading complex initiatives across distributed teams and influencing senior stakeholders without relying on direct reporting relationships.

  • Enjoy coaching and developing colleagues, sharing expertise and helping teams build effective agency partnerships.

  • Thrive in ambiguous, fast-changing environments and enjoy building new commercial models, processes and partnerships from the ground up.

  • Are passionate about AI and excited by the opportunity to shape how agencies and advertisers adopt transformative technologies responsibly at scale.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

About the Team

OpenAI’s GTM Partnerships team builds a strategic, global partner ecosystem to accelerate customer success, enable responsible enterprise AI adoption, and drive durable growth in support of OpenAI’s mission. We work cross-functionally across Sales, Solutions, Product, Engineering, Security, Legal, Finance, Marketing, Operations, and Customer Success to translate strategic partnerships into measurable outcomes for customers.

Global consulting and technology partners help enterprises move from AI strategy to production deployment. This role will lead OpenAI’s partnership with BCG across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa (EMEA), bringing together BCG’s industry, consulting, technology, and delivery expertise with OpenAI’s products and capabilities. You will turn the global alliance strategy into a focused EMEA business plan and repeatable field execution that delivers customer and commercial impact.

About the Role

The Partner Director, BCG EMEA will lead OpenAI’s partner business with BCG across the region. You will own the EMEA joint business plan, build executive alignment, and activate BCG and OpenAI field teams to generate qualified pipeline, win strategic opportunities, and drive successful production adoption. You will align regional priorities and execution with the global BCG alliance strategy.

This is a strategic and hands-on leadership role. You will connect senior executive engagement with joint account planning, co-selling, solution and delivery alignment, field enablement, governance, and day-to-day execution. Success requires a strong understanding of how a large, matrixed professional-services organisation operates, commercial discipline, technical fluency, and the ability to align teams without formal authority.

The ideal candidate has led a high-impact partnership with strategic partners, built measurable pipeline and customer outcomes across EMEA, and knows how to turn alliance strategy into account-level execution and successful deployments.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the EMEA partnership with BCG, including regional strategy, executive alignment, joint planning, pipeline growth, customer outcomes, delivery quality, and long-term expansion, in alignment with the global alliance.

  • Develop and execute an EMEA joint business plan with clear account and industry priorities, investments, decision rights, milestones, and measures of success.

  • Build trusted relationships with BCG’s EMEA leadership, industry and functional leaders, alliance teams, client account leaders, sales organizations, architects, and delivery leaders, while staying aligned with global stakeholders.

  • Translate executive priorities into repeatable field execution spanning account mapping, opportunity qualification, co-selling, solution development, technical engagement, delivery handoffs, and escalation.

  • Shape joint solutions and industry plays that combine OpenAI products and capabilities with BCG’s consulting, technology, data, security, governance, and delivery strengths.

  • Lead joint account planning and strategic customer pursuits with BCG and OpenAI field teams across EMEA, with particular focus on complex and regulated enterprises.

  • Create a clear engagement model for OpenAI sellers and technical teams, including when to involve BCG, how opportunities are qualified, who owns each step, and how channel conflict is resolved.

  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Solutions, Security, Legal, Finance, and Commercial teams to support complex customer engagements and remove technical, contractual, compliance, and operational blockers.

  • Build BCG’s EMEA field and delivery readiness through executive sponsorship, sales enablement, technical training, reusable solution patterns, and disciplined delivery handoffs.

  • Establish regional governance across executive business reviews, pipeline inspection, forecasting, milestone tracking, performance reporting, and escalation, connected to the global alliance operating model.

  • Set and monitor EMEA partnership KPIs, including qualified pipeline, conversion, production adoption, customer value, partner readiness, delivery quality, and return on OpenAI investment.

  • Prioritise OpenAI resources for EMEA opportunities with the greatest strategic value, commercial potential, customer impact, delivery readiness, and repeatability.

  • Represent OpenAI in senior partner, customer, and industry engagements with clarity, sound judgment, and strong executive presence.

  • Build the regional operating model and identify the team capacity needed to scale the BCG partnership across EMEA.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • Significant experience leading strategic alliances, GSI, or advisory partnerships, ecosystem sales, business development, or enterprise go-to-market programs in AI, cloud, data, SaaS, or enterprise technology.

  • Direct experience working with BCG and deep familiarity with its EMEA organization, incentives, decision-making networks, commercial model, industry and functional practices, and enterprise delivery motions.

  • A proven record of leading a multi-year partnership or regional alliance business with measurable pipeline, revenue, adoption, deployment, or customer outcomes.

  • Experience designing and scaling joint operating models across large, matrixed organisations, including governance, account planning, incentives, staffing, delivery handoffs, and escalation.

  • Demonstrated success shaping and advancing complex C-suite enterprise transformation opportunities from strategy through production deployment.

  • Strong executive presence and the ability to build credibility with senior BCG and customer leaders while remaining close to operating details.

  • Commercial judgment and experience prioritizing investments, qualifying opportunities, managing forecasts, and making clear tradeoffs.

  • Technical fluency across enterprise AI, cloud environments, data platforms, security, governance, risk, and modern application architectures.

  • Strong cross-functional leadership and the ability to align Sales, Solutions, Product, Engineering, Security, Legal, Finance, Marketing, and Operations without direct authority.

  • Experience building partner enablement, joint solutions, industry plays, and scalable field engagement models across EMEA.

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity and creating structure, accountability, and momentum in a rapidly evolving market.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, negotiation, and executive presentation skills.

  • A builder mindset, high ownership, low ego, and a consistent focus on customer value and responsible AI adoption.

  • OpenAI and BCG have a clear EMEA growth strategy, differentiated joint value proposition, executive governance model, and measurable business plan aligned with the global alliance.

  • Joint solution patterns and industry plays become repeatable rather than remaining bespoke.

  • OpenAI resources are allocated transparently toward the highest-impact opportunities.

raw.description:
About the Team

The HR Business Partner team at OpenAI supports managers and employees as teams grow, perform and adapt. We work alongside managers at all levels to resolve day-to-day people challenges, build management capability and create the conditions for teams to do their best work.

Our expertise spans team effectiveness, talent development, manager coaching, employee relations and change management, grounded in our Contributions & Impact (C&I) culture. We operate with urgency, empathy and sound judgment, valuing sincerity, collaboration and meaningful impact.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Senior HR Business Partner to support managers and teams across EMEA, with a primary focus on Go-to-Market and responsibility for selected other functions in the region. You’ll provide hands-on support to managers at all levels, owning day-to-day people work and helping teams grow and scale effectively.

Your GTM partnership will span teams such as Sales, Technical Success, Partnerships and Marketing. Across your portfolio, you’ll build a deep understanding of business priorities and use that context to prioritise and deliver practical people support.

As a hands-on partner to managers at all levels, you will use independent judgment to coach managers, resolve people issues and follow through on day-to-day work as teams scale. You will own delivery across your portfolio, working closely with the International HRBP Leader, Recruiting, Finance, Employment Legal and People centres of expertise, and involving specialist partners when needed.

This is an individual contributor role reporting to the International HRBP Leader.

Your Key Responsibilities

  • Own day-to-day HRBP support with a primary focus on GTM. Be a practical point of contact for managers on performance, employee relations, team changes and development. Prioritise issues, agree clear next steps and see them through to resolution as teams scale.

  • Support teams as they grow. Help managers put agreed team structures and workforce plans into practice, clarify roles and address capacity needs as teams enter new markets and scale existing operations. Coordinate with Finance and Recruiting to support hiring and team changes.

  • Build manager effectiveness. Coach managers at all levels, from first-time managers to experienced people managers, on feedback, difficult conversations, team dynamics and accountability. Help them address everyday people challenges with clarity and care.

  • Build capability and succession. Help managers identify skills and development needs across GTM teams. Partner on talent reviews, succession planning, internal mobility and development, with particular attention to roles essential to customer and business outcomes.

  • Drive performance and rewards decisions. Help managers set clear expectations, address underperformance and recognise contributions consistently. Partner with Compensation and Sales Compensation specialists on people implications of incentive structures, role changes and rewards decisions.

  • Lead through regional complexity. Guide organisational changes and sensitive employee matters across EMEA, partnering with Employment Legal and Employee Relations specialists. Balance business urgency, local requirements and fair, consistent treatment.

  • Use insight to act early. Combine workforce data, business context and employee feedback to identify emerging risks, test assumptions and recommend action. Track whether interventions improve capability, retention and team effectiveness.

  • Scale effective People practices. Partner with global HRBPs and centres of expertise to evolve performance, engagement and talent programmes for EMEA, ensuring regional needs inform global decisions and local delivery remains practical.

What You Bring

  • Substantial HRBP experience. Typically 7–10+ years in HR, including at least five years supporting managers and teams in high-growth, international or complex organisations. We value the scope and impact of your experience.

  • Commercial understanding. Experience supporting Sales and other go-to-market functions, with an understanding of enterprise sales cycles, customer-facing roles and the people implications of commercial operating models.

  • Hands-on manager partnership. A record of supporting managers at all levels, resolving day-to-day people issues and owning delivery across a busy portfolio. You can exercise independent judgment, challenge constructively and build trusted relationships.

  • EMEA experience. Experience across multiple EMEA markets, navigating cultural differences and varied employment environments, with sound judgment about when to involve specialist partners.

  • Organisational and talent judgment. Practical experience supporting team growth, workforce planning, manager coaching, performance management and talent development, including delivering change through ambiguity.

  • Analytical and execution strength. The ability to diagnose problems using data and context, make clear recommendations and follow through. You prioritise effectively, take ownership of complex people issues and stay close to the details through resolution.

  • Integrity and care. Discretion with sensitive matters, fairness in decision-making and a willingness to listen, adapt and act with conviction.

Workplace and Location

This role is based in London. We operate a hybrid model with three days per week in the office and offer relocation support where appropriate.

This is how we have become one of the 500 fastest-growing tech companies in North America for the seventh year in a row, as ranked by Deloitte!

Why This Role is Exciting

We are looking for an intelligent, coachable, hard-working, and driven professional to lead a team of Account Executives to sell Optro products into our Commercial segment. The Area Director, Sales will lead, coach and develop a team of 5-7 sales professionals to proactively generate new opportunities into target accounts, close business to achieve quarterly and annual revenue goals, and will report to the Vice President of EMEA.

Location: London, UK (Hybrid role ~2-3 days/week in the office in central London)


Key Responsibilities

raw.title: Information Security Engineer - Infrastructure Security
raw.description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

The Role

We're looking for an Information Security Engineer who can think broadly about how infrastructure is built, attacked, defended, and improved. You may have deep experience in one area—such as endpoint security, Active Directory, Data Loss Prevention, cloud security, identity, or detection and response—but you’re motivated by solving security problems across the environment.

As an Information Security Engineer focused on infrastructure security, you'll help protect Palantir's global endpoints, servers, identity systems, applications, networks, and data flows. You'll work across teams to reduce attack surface, improve defensive controls, investigate security events, and turn security findings into durable architectural and operational improvements.

This is not just a corporate security role; the adversaries we face are sophisticated. We need someone who understands both the details and the broader system: how a weakness in one part of the environment can create risk somewhere else, how controls interact, and how to build security improvements that hold up in practice.

Core Responsibilities
  • Design, implement, and improve security controls across endpoints, servers, identity systems, cloud services, SaaS applications, networks, and data flows.
  • Drive security posture improvements through hardening standards, configuration management, vulnerability remediation, access controls, monitoring, and ongoing validation.
  • Assess security risks in new platforms, products, architectures, vendors, and services, and turn findings into practical recommendations and engineering work.
  • Build and maintain automation for security operations, including configuration validation, drift monitoring, patching, access reviews, policy enforcement, alert triage, and security hygiene.
  • Partner with Identity, Infrastructure, Engineering, Legal, and other Information Security teams to strengthen security architecture and address recurring risks.
  • Turn insights from assessments, red team exercises, incident investigations, and operational reviews into durable fixes, such as configuration changes, architectural improvements, policy updates, and automation.
  • Build expertise in one or more security domains while contributing across the broader infrastructure security lifecycle.

    • What We're Looking For
  • Experience securing one or more major infrastructure domains, such as Windows, macOS, Linux, Active Directory, cloud platforms, SaaS applications, networking, identity systems, or enterprise endpoints.
  • A broad infrastructure security mindset and curiosity about systems beyond your primary area of expertise.
  • Familiarity with common infrastructure attack paths, adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures, and the controls used to prevent, detect, and contain them.
  • The ability to assess complex environments and recognize how weaknesses across identity, endpoints, applications, networks, cloud services, or data flows can combine to create risk.
  • Experience evaluating security tools and validating that controls are deployed effectively and continue to work as intended.
  • Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code, configuration management, CI/CD, or other approaches to making security controls repeatable and scalable.

    • What We Value
  • The ability to own projects, make progress through ambiguity, and balance competing priorities while working well with colleagues.
  • Experience in complex, high-assurance, regulated, or rapidly changing environments.
  • Comfort moving between strategic problem-solving and hands-on technical work.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical risks and work with partner teams to drive remediation.
  • Contributions to security programs, tooling, automation, incident investigations, or technical research—whether public or internal.

    • What We Require
  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in information security, infrastructure security, security engineering, security operations, or a closely related field.
  • Demonstrated experience securing at least one major infrastructure or security domain, with the ability and interest to work across multiple domains.
  • Active TS/SCI security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain one.
  • A strong sense of ownership, sound judgment, and integrity.
    • Life at Palantir
     
    We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Paying attention to the needs of our community enables us to optimize our opportunities to grow and helps ensure many pathways to success at Palantir. Promoting health and well-being across all areas of Palantirians’ lives is just one of the ways we’re investing in our community. Learn more at Life at Palantir and note that our offerings may vary by region.
     
    In keeping consistent with Palantir’s values and culture, we believe employees are “better together” and in-person work affords the opportunity for more creative outcomes. Therefore, we encourage employees to work from our offices to foster connectivity and innovation. Many teams do offer hybrid options (WFH a day or two a week), allowing our employees to strike the right trade-off for their personal productivity. Based on business need, there are a few roles that allow for “Remote” work on an exceptional basis. If you are applying for one of these roles, you must work from the city and or country in which you are employed. If the posting is specified as Onsite, you are required to work from an office.
     
    If you want to empower the world's most important institutions, you belong here. Palantir values excellence regardless of background. We are committed to making the application and hiring process accessible to everyone and will provide a reasonable accommodation for those living with a disability. If you need an accommodation for the application or hiring process, please and let us know how we can help.
     
    Please note that you will never be asked to submit a payment or share financial information to participate in our interview process. If you suspect that you've been contacted by a scammer, we recommend you cease all communication with the individual and consider reporting them to the relevant authorities, such as the US FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3).

  • Drive security posture improvements through hardening standards, configuration management, vulnerability remediation, access controls, monitoring, and ongoing validation.
  • Assess security risks in new platforms, products, architectures, vendors, and services, and turn findings into practical recommendations and engineering work.
  • Build and maintain automation for security operations, including configuration validation, drift monitoring, patching, access reviews, policy enforcement, alert triage, and security hygiene.
  • Partner with Identity, Infrastructure, Engineering, Legal, and other Information Security teams to strengthen security architecture and address recurring risks.
  • Turn insights from assessments, red team exercises, incident investigations, and operational reviews into durable fixes, such as configuration changes, architectural improvements, policy updates, and automation.
  • Build expertise in one or more security domains while contributing across the broader infrastructure security lifecycle.

    • What We're Looking For
  • Experience securing one or more major infrastructure domains, such as Windows, macOS, Linux, Active Directory, cloud platforms, SaaS applications, networking, identity systems, or enterprise endpoints.
  • A broad infrastructure security mindset and curiosity about systems beyond your primary area of expertise.
  • Familiarity with common infrastructure attack paths, adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures, and the controls used to prevent, detect, and contain them.
  • The ability to assess complex environments and recognize how weaknesses across identity, endpoints, applications, networks, cloud services, or data flows can combine to create risk.
  • Experience evaluating security tools and validating that controls are deployed effectively and continue to work as intended.
  • Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code, configuration management, CI/CD, or other approaches to making security controls repeatable and scalable.

    • What We Value
  • The ability to own projects, make progress through ambiguity, and balance competing priorities while working well with colleagues.
  • Experience in complex, high-assurance, regulated, or rapidly changing environments.
  • Comfort moving between strategic problem-solving and hands-on technical work.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical risks and work with partner teams to drive remediation.
  • Contributions to security programs, tooling, automation, incident investigations, or technical research—whether public or internal.

    • What We Require
  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in information security, infrastructure security, security engineering, security operations, or a closely related field.
  • Demonstrated experience securing at least one major infrastructure or security domain, with the ability and interest to work across multiple domains.
  • Active TS/SCI security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain one.
  • A strong sense of ownership, sound judgment, and integrity.

raw.description:
Graduate Sales Development Representative (Life Sciences)

 

➡️ Have a degree in Life Sciences and looking for an alternative to the lab where you can still use your scientific knowledge every day?

➡️ Excited by the opportunity to work with leading pharmaceutical, biotech and medical device companies, helping them accelerate innovation through AI?

➡️ Want to build a rewarding career in tech sales with exceptional training, uncapped commission and a clear path to becoming an Account Executive?

If this sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you.

Role Summary:

We're looking for ambitious graduates and early-career professionals with a background in Life Sciences to join PatSnap as a Sales Development Representative (SDR).

This is your chance to take your scientific knowledge beyond the lab and apply it in a commercial role, working with some of the world's most innovative pharmaceutical, biotech and medical device organisations.

You'll become a trusted first point of contact for R&D and innovation leaders, introducing PatSnap's AI-powered platform and helping organisations accelerate research, reduce development risk and bring life-changing innovations to market faster.

We're not looking for experienced salespeople, we're looking for curious, ambitious graduates who are eager to learn. We'll provide structured training, ongoing coaching and mentorship to help you develop into a high-performing SaaS sales professional.

This is a fast-paced, target-driven role where your success will be determined by your resilience, curiosity and willingness to learn. If you're motivated by personal growth, enjoy speaking with people and want to build a career with exceptional earning potential, this could be the perfect opportunity.

This is a hybrid role based in our London office, with the flexibility to work either hybrid (Monday, Tuesday and Thursday in the office) or fully office-based if you prefer.

 

Who are we?

PatSnap is a global, Series E, unicorn SaaS platform that transforms the way organizations harness their Intellectual Property and Research & Development productivity. Our user-friendly platform revolutionizes how IP and R&D teams collaborate across the entire innovation lifecycle — using industry-leading, domain-specific AI to generate and validate ideas and bring innovative products to market faster, better, and cheaper. More than 12,000 R&D and IP teams worldwide use and trust PatSnap to innovate and commercialize new products.

 

As the leading global Life Sciences intelligence platform, PatSnap helps pharmaceutical, biotech, medical device, and life sciences organisations make better innovation decisions. By connecting patents, scientific literature, clinical trials, regulatory data, and market intelligence, we enable our customers to identify white spaces, reduce R&D risk, and accelerate breakthrough innovation.

 

We have a vibrant and diverse team with offices in Toronto, London, Shanghai, and Singapore. Our hyper-growth trajectory is powered by our people, and we are extremely proud of our company-wide vision, work ethic, and entrepreneurial spirit. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment where talent thrives and ideas bloom.

What You'll Be Doing:

As an SDR, you'll be on the front line of PatSnap's growth, helping us connect with the world's leading pharmaceutical, biotech and medical device organisations. This is a true business development role where you'll learn how to identify opportunities, build relationships and create commercial value. Sales isn't about having all the answers, it's about asking great questions. Your scientific curiosity will help you understand customer challenges, while we'll teach you the commercial skills to build a successful career in SaaS sales.

You will:

  • Develop a hunter mindset, proactively identifying and engaging new prospects through phone, email and LinkedIn.

  • Use your scientific background to build credibility with senior R&D, innovation and scientific leaders.

  • Create and qualify new sales opportunities, turning cold prospects into valuable commercial conversations.

  • Build resilience by handling rejection positively and consistently achieving ambitious activity and pipeline targets.

  • Work closely with experienced Account Executives, helping convert qualified opportunities into revenue while learning every stage of the sales process.

  • Develop the commercial skills needed to progress into a closing role, including influencing, negotiation and relationship building.


What We'd Love From You

You don't need previous sales experience – we're looking for people with the attitude, curiosity and ambition to build a successful career in SaaS sales.

We're looking for someone who:

  • Has a degree (or equivalent experience) in Life Sciences or a related scientific discipline.

  • Is excited by the idea of applying your scientific knowledge in a commercial, customer-facing role.

  • Ambitious and motivated by success, with the drive to excel in an uncapped commission environment.

  • Confident and proactive, comfortable starting conversations and building relationships with new people.

  • Resilient and determined, with the mindset to overcome challenges and thrive in a target-driven environment.

  • Naturally competitive, with a strong desire to achieve goals and progress quickly in your career.

  • An excellent communicator, able to explain complex scientific concepts in a simple, engaging way.

  • Curious, coachable and eager to learn, always looking for ways to improve.

  • Organised and self-motivated, with the ability to manage your time and priorities effectively.

  • Passionate about technology, AI and innovation, and excited by the impact they have on R&D and scientific discovery.

  • A natural problem solver who enjoys understanding customers' challenges and helping them find solutions.

  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, collaborative environment where no two days are the same.

Benefits & Perks:

A genuinely strong sales culture we’re really proud of. High-performing but low ego, social, and dynamic. It’s a team that supports each other, shares best practice, raises standards, and celebrates wins properly together. Alongside a great product, it’s one of the best parts of working here.

Additional benefits

  • 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays

  • Two paid volunteering days

  • Private healthcare with AXA

  • Pension with Scottish Widows

  • Enhanced parental leave policies

  • Work from home stipend

  • Cycle to Work scheme

  • Life assurance

  • Payroll giving options

  • Eyecare vouchers

Base Salary: £28,330

Commission: £18,887

On-Target Earnings Total (OTE): £47,217 (60/40 split)

High achievers regularly exceed target, with earnings of £60k+
