raw.title: Product Security Engineer
raw.description:
Orbital is the AI platform for real estate legal work.

Real estate shapes the world around us: our homes, our workplaces and our cultural landmarks. It’s the infrastructure that powers everyday life and is the world's largest asset class. Yet behind every single deal, real estate and legal teams work hard to navigate decades-old complexity; manually connecting documents, hidden obligations, geo-spatial context, and multiple parties into a path forward. We connect the legal and physical record, so that path is clearer than ever before. Our mission is to make real estate transactions faster, clearer, and less manual.

Here, you'll be part of changing how the deals behind the largest asset class get transacted, and will help shape the future of real estate.

A bit about us:

🚀 We’re building at the forefront of AI technology, without losing the deeply human expertise our clients depend on.

🏢 Orbital is built with former practising real estate lawyers and 250+ years of combined legal expertise. We're purpose-built for the complexity of real estate: accelerating due diligence, drafting and negotiation, and deal coordination with legal-grade precision.

💰 We've just raised a $60m Series B, led by Brighton Park Capital, to accelerate our global expansion – $75m raised to date.

🤝 We're trusted by 5,000+ real estate professionals, spanning UK Magic Circle and US Am Law 100 firms, to household names like M&S. Leading firms like BCLP, Orrick, Goodwin, Womble Bond Dickinson and Clifford Chance rely on Orbital to remove the busywork, freeing legal and real estate teams to focus on sharp judgment, standout client service, and closing deals faster.

💡 Working at Orbital means joining a bold, ambitious team, with the trust to take ownership and make a real impact from day one.

Role Overview 🔎

We're looking for a Product Security Engineer to own the security of Orbital's product: the AI agent our customers use, the platform it runs on, and how we build both.

Our customers are law firms and real estate businesses. They trust us with confidential transaction documents, and they ask hard questions about how we protect them. Our product is an AI agent that reads those documents, calls tools and runs code on a lawyer's behalf. That brings the usual cloud security work and a newer set of risks: prompt injection, agents acting on untrusted input, and attackers using AI to move faster than before.

You'll be our first in-house product security engineer, taking on work we have so far relied on contractors for. You'll build security into the product rather than review it from outside: you'll decide how we rate a vulnerability and how fast we act on it, build the automated systems that find and fix issues before an attacker does, and set the security bar that engineering builds to. You'll work alongside our product engineers, with the authority to require changes across teams on security grounds, independent of any one team's delivery deadlines. An information security lead will own company-wide policy, compliance and customer assurance, and you'll work closely with them.

You won't start from zero. Our AWS environment follows the Well-Architected Framework, with GuardDuty, Security Hub, encryption at rest and scoped credentials in place, and we hold SOC 2 and ISO 27001 commitments to our customers. What we need is someone to own it, find the gaps, and raise the standard as the company and the threat landscape grow.

You'll get a chance to 👩‍💻 👨‍💻

  • Build an automated security harness. Put agents to work on our product: continuous red-team and blue-team loops that probe the agent, the platform and our code, find vulnerabilities, and propose or ship the fix. Manual review should be justified when required and automatic harness improvement is expected.

  • Own vulnerability management end to end. Define how we classify severity and the response time each level demands, so a critical CVE gets fixed the same day. Automate patching, dependency and image scanning, and make sure findings reach an owner and get closed.

  • Secure an AI agent in production. Threat-model how our agent handles untrusted documents, emails and web content, and the tools and sandboxes it uses. Design defences against prompt injection and data exfiltration, and test them.

  • Make security part of how we build. Review designs and changes that touch authentication, tenant isolation, secrets and data handling. Turn recurring findings into automated checks so the protection holds without depending on someone remembering.

  • Respond to security incidents. Lead the technical response when something goes wrong: containment, investigation and the fix. Build the technical side of our breach playbooks with our information security lead, and run the review afterwards.

  • Choose and run our security tooling. Evaluate and roll out a cloud security platform (such as Wiz) and the detection, alerting and logging we need across AWS and Azure. As our only product security specialist, use tooling and AI agents to cover more ground than one person could alone.

  • Test our defences. Run red-team exercises, manage external penetration testers, and run breach drills with engineering so everyone knows their part before it matters.

  • Close the loop on findings. Fix what penetration tests and security researchers report to us, run responsible disclosure, and keep the technical evidence for our SOC 2 and ISO 27001 controls current, working with our information security lead.

  • Make the work visible. Show leadership and engineering what the harness finds, what has been fixed and what risk remains, in plain language, with a recommendation for each open risk.

You should apply if you ✍️

  • You build with agents. You'd rather put an agent loop on a problem than repeat a manual review. You've used AI agents to find, triage or fix security issues, and you aim for automation that leaves people to review only the exceptions.

  • You have deep, hands-on security engineering experience. You've owned security for a cloud-native product or platform and can do the work yourself, from reading code and IAM policies to configuring detection and running an investigation.

  • You know AWS security well. IAM, network design, KMS, GuardDuty, Security Hub, CloudTrail and how they fit together in a real production environment.

  • You've led incident response. You've run a real security incident, including containment, investigation, communication and the follow-up, and you stay clear-headed under pressure.

  • You take application and AI security seriously. You understand OWASP-class vulnerabilities, and you're interested in the new risks that come with LLM agents, such as prompt injection and over-broad tool access.

  • You understand the product and the business. You know why a finding matters to our customers and our commercial position. You can tell a theoretical finding from one that puts customer data at risk, you spend effort where the risk is real, and you don't disappear down technical rabbit holes.

  • You help teams ship safely. You find the secure way to do what the team needs, and you block work only when the risk justifies it. When you do, you explain why clearly enough that engineers understand and agree.

  • You work independently. As our first in-house product security engineer, you'll set your own priorities, build the programme, and know when to bring in outside help.

  • You bring people with you. You can explain a security risk to an engineer, a lawyer and a board member, adjusting the detail for each, and you change how teams work through influence rather than authority.

You'll most likely come from a security engineering, product security or application security role at a fast-growing startup, or from a security consultancy with hands-on delivery. We're open to different backgrounds if you can show the depth, judgement and automation-first approach this role needs.

It would also be nice if you have

  • Experience securing LLM or agentic AI applications, or research into prompt injection and AI-specific threats.

  • Harness engineering experience: building the tooling, evaluation loops and guardrails that let AI agents do real engineering work.

  • Hands-on experience with SOC 2 and ISO 27001 audits.

  • Experience with Azure, Kubernetes or container security, or sandboxed code execution.

  • Familiarity with identity and SSO providers such as WorkOS or Okta.

  • Experience in legal, financial or other regulated industries.

🔒 Security is everyone’s responsibility at Orbital. We ask all team members to follow our security policies, complete regular awareness training, and handle sensitive data with care in line with ISO 27001 standards. Spot something unusual? Reporting risks or incidents quickly helps us maintain the strong culture of security and compliance we all depend on.

💡 At Orbital, we’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We especially welcome applications from people who are traditionally underrepresented in tech. Even if you don’t meet every single requirement, or if the right role isn’t listed yet, we’d still love to hear from you.

💰 This hiring range is a reasonable estimate of the base pay range for this position at the time of posting. Pay is based on several factors, which may include job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and business requirements.

Everyone who works with Orbital goes through background screening before they start. It's part of how we keep Orbital secure, for the people who work here and for the client information we're trusted with.

raw.title: Design Engineer
raw.description:
Since early 2024, we've gone from 0 to over 900 customers, succeeding where many have tried and failed before. We have a big mission: to make it wildly easier and more profitable to run and grow a renewables installation business, and through that to make a real dent in the world's carbon emissions and a far better experience for homeowners.

We're now looking for a Design Engineer who wants to design & ship exceptional outcomes for users. Most of our product is a front end over hard physics (heat-loss calculations, hydronic design, LiDAR floor plans, compliance that has to be right), used by installers on a phone, with no signal, in a hurry. Making that feel simple is a design problem and an engineering problem at the same time, and this role sits right on that seam.

 

🌲 About Spruce

  • Almost 20% of the UK's carbon emissions comes from heating homes – there's simply no way to reach net zero without phasing out gas and oil boilers. Right now the only serious alternative is heat pumps, with their almost-magical ability to turn 1 kW of electricity into 3-5 kW of heat (🤯). But the heat pump installation journey is slow, inefficient, and just so painful. This makes it hard for existing installers to grow their businesses and puts off gas engineers from starting to do heat pumps. Perhaps most critically, it means you can't currently offer a heat pump when someone's boiler breaks and they urgently need heating.

  • We're fixing this. We've built a platform for heat pump installers to manage the whole installation journey from initial enquiry through to final compliance paperwork, freeing up their time to focus on what really matters: doing high-quality installations, providing great customer service, and scaling their business. Despite only getting started at the beginning of 2024, we're having a massive impact on installation businesses, suppliers, and manufacturers across the UK: halving the time they spend on each job and doubling their sales conversion rates.

  • We raised a chunky Seed round last year from top-tier investors and this year have grown the team 3x and revenue 4x. We've expanded into Ireland, are launching an end-to-end solar and battery product in November, and are increasingly becoming the operating system for the whole home renewables supply chain. If you can picture a combination of ServiceTitan, Procore, and AutoCAD, you might get a sense of where we're headed…

 

🥖 The role

You'll own how the product looks, feels and behaves wherever installers use it, from the first sketch to the shipped feature. Installers only adopt Spruce if it's easy to use on a real job, and adoption is what drives our growth. That puts your work at the centre of the business. Day-to-day you'll be:

  • Designing and shipping – You'll take a flow from rough idea all the way to production, prototyping in whatever gets you to an answer fastest (often code, sometimes Figma or a sketch), and testing with installers as you go. The gap between "we should fix this" and "it's fixed" is often a day.

  • Owning the interaction layer – You'll build and look after the component library and the patterns underneath it: motion, loading and empty states, touch targets that still work with gloves on. The small things that make a complex tool feel simple.

  • Building the parts that are hard to get right – The canvas-based floor plan and system design tools, the offline survey app (incl. LiDAR), the proposals homeowners see. These are the parts where the UI is the product, and where we've got the most still to build.

  • Raising the bar on everything we ship – You'll work closely with our product designers and developers, pairing on their work and reviewing it, so the quality of what you build rubs off on the rest of the product.

  • Spending time with installers – You'll go out on site, watch how the product actually gets used, then come back and change it.

You'll report to Steph, our co-founder and CPO (she’s pretty awesome) and you’ll work alongside Dan & Arron who’ve cooked up some incredible work in their time so far.

 

🫵 About you

We look for the same five things in everyone at Spruce: curiosity; intense drive, ambition and work ethic; a high degree of personal agency and ownership; deep humility and a growth mindset; and excellent craft. You might currently call yourself a designer who ships, a front-end engineer with strong design instincts, or already a design engineer. We're looking for 3+ years of experience (and potentially a lot more) designing and building product UI, ideally in a startup or a fast-paced, impact-focussed team. We'd love to speak with you if you have:

  • Real taste, and shipped work to prove it – You can show us production UI you designed and built, and talk about why the details are the way they are. Work you'd happily put next to the best-crafted B2B products out there.

  • Strong design craft, and a real appetite for code – You're a strong designer first. You don't need to be a front-end engineer, and you might well ship with Cursor or Claude Code, but you want to understand the code you're shipping. Bonus for React and TypeScript depth, canvas/WebGL, animation, or complex state on mobile.

  • A prototyping instinct – You'd rather build a rough version and test it than argue about it in a doc. You're comfortable with things being imperfect in front of users.

  • Systems thinking – You enjoy the structure of a good component library and understand that consistency is what lets a small team ship fast. You also know when to slow down first: you value time spent on lo-fi wireframes and on understanding the data model before anything gets polished.

  • Curiosity about the domain – You want to understand how heating systems, solar and battery actually work, and you pick up technical detail fast. By the end of week two you'll be arguing about the best way to show a homeowner their solar self-consumption.

 

🌟 Our offer

  • 💰 £60-110k salary, depending on experience and location

  • 🍰 Meaningful slice of equity (options) in the company

  • 🏖️ 33 days holiday (25 plus bank holidays) and opportunity to work from abroad for another 30 days each year

  • 🏡 Hybrid working: 2–3 days in-person a week (London or Bristol), with full-team meetups every fortnight

  • 🏥 Private Medical Cover (Vitality)

  • 👧 Workplace Nursery Benefit scheme (YellowNest)

  • 🧑‍🍼 Enhanced Parental Leave

  • 🚲 Cycle to Work scheme

  • 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Brilliant team to learn from and massive opportunity to grow

 

🧑‍💻 Working at Spruce

  • We're currently a close-knit team of 34, split between London and Bristol. We spend 2-3 days each week working together in-person in both locations, and get everyone together every fortnight.

  • You'll have genuine influence from day one. The best idea wins regardless of seniority. We expect you to challenge everything, ask "why?" multiple levels deep, and push back when something doesn't make sense.

  • We want everyone to spend time with installers on-site, feel their pain points, then be able to rapidly suggest and implement solutions based on real feedback rather than assumptions. This is clearly particularly important for this role but you'll be surrounded by a whole team who are also close to our customers.

  • We move fast and ship imperfect things, learning from users rather than trying to perfect in isolation. When things break, we focus on how we fix it, what we can learn, and never blame. You'll own your outcomes whilst knowing the team has your back.

  • Feedback is constant, direct, and kind. We'll tell you when something isn't working and expect the same honesty (and empathy) back.

Compensation: £60K – £110K • Offers Equity

About us

At Trainline, our purpose is to empower greener travel choices, connecting people and places. Trainline enables millions of travellers to find and book the best value tickets across carriers, fares, and journey options through our highly rated mobile app, website, and B2B partner channels. 

Great journeys start with Trainline 🚄 

We’re Europe’s leading independent rail platform, helping millions of travellers find and book the best-value rail and coach journeys across our app, website and partner channels.

Our job is to make the green travel choice the best choice. By building a better train travel experience, we help more people choose rail - creating a positive impact for customers, our business and the planet.

We’re a team of more than 1,000 Trainliners from over 50 nationalities, working across London, Paris, Barcelona, Milan, Edinburgh and Madrid. Now is a brilliant time to join us and help shape the future of travel.

Introducing the GRC team 👋

Trainline is investing in the next stage of our security programme, and we’re looking for a Security GRC Associate to help strengthen how we manage third-party security risk and assurance.

You’ll join our Information Security team, reporting to the GRC Manager. raw.title: Senior AI Engineer
raw.description:
UFORCE exists to make aggression unaffordable.

Founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, UFORCE is a defence-technology company with operations across Europe, the United States and Asia.

UFORCE builds uncrewed vessels, ground robotics and aircraft, autonomy software, and the command-and-control layer that operates them together. Each platform is deployable on its own, and stronger as part of the system. Its product lines include the MAGURA family of uncrewed surface vessels, the NEMESIS family of strike platforms, the LIUT family of ground robotic platforms, and counter-UAS systems.

About the role

The Senior Engineer, AI / ML — Self-Serve Toolchain will build the end-to-end system that lets customers adapt UFORCE models on their own private data without exposing that data to us.

This role spans data processing, foundation-model-assisted labeling, human-in-the-loop QA, active learning, training, evaluation, and model promotion. You will turn an in-flight principal-led capability into a repeatable toolchain that non-expert customers can run safely on-site.

What you’ll do

 

  • Own the ML adaptation pipeline from raw customer data to trained, evaluated, deployable models.

  • Build foundation-model-assisted labeling workflows using tools such as SAM-2, Grounding DINO, open-vocabulary models, LLM steering, and human review.

  • Design self-serve operator workflows using yes/no/maybe feedback and natural-language corrections.

  • Create versioned datasets with lineage, data cards, label provenance, class distributions, and known gaps.

  • Build QA methods that catch systematic pseudo-label errors, missing annotations, and long-tail data gaps.

  • Develop active-learning loops that prioritize the highest-value frames for limited operator review.

  • Build reproducible train/eval pipelines with experiment tracking, model packaging, and promotion gates.

  • Design evaluation around held-out anchor sets, leakage prevention, baselines, slice metrics, and automated approve/reject decisions.

  • Package the toolchain for on-prem, air-gapped, regulated, or customer-held environments.

  • Close the field-failure loop by feeding live failures back into the next tune cycle.

  • Lead and grow a small specialist team around curation, auto-labeling, deployment, and onboarding.

What success looks like

 

  • Customers can run a full adaptation cycle without engineer intervention.

  • Customer data stays inside the customer boundary.

  • The system produces trusted datasets with clear provenance and quality signals.

  • Pseudo-label quality is measured and systematic errors are caught early.

  • The promotion gate can approve or reject models based on evidence, not intuition.

  • Evaluation is protected by anchor sets, leakage controls, slice metrics, and baseline comparisons.

  • Field failures become reproducible inputs to the next training cycle.

  • Synthetic data is used only when it proves value against real held-out data.

  • The toolchain becomes a repeatable capability supported by a small, ramped team.

Required Qualifications

 

  • 5+ years building production ML, AI, or computer-vision systems.

  • Strong Python and PyTorch.

  • Experience owning ML data pipelines, training pipelines, or evaluation infrastructure.

  • Deep CV data experience: detection, segmentation, annotation taxonomies, dataset curation, and data quality.

  • Hands-on experience with model-in-the-loop or foundation-model-assisted labeling.

  • Familiarity with tools such as SAM-2, Grounding DINO, FiftyOne, and annotation platforms.

  • Strong understanding of evaluation: held-out sets, leakage prevention, baselines, slice metrics, and promotion gates.

  • Experience with QA sampling, label-noise analysis, missing annotations, IAA, or alternatives when only one operator is available.

  • Experience with active learning or other methods for prioritizing labeling effort.

  • Ability to reason about dataset economics: quality vs. quantity, long-tail coverage, and cost-per-useful-example.

  • Experience with dataset versioning, lineage, experiment tracking, model registries, or data cards.

  • Strong ownership, communication, and systems thinking.

  • Experience leading engineers as a tech lead, staff engineer, or small-team manager.

Nice to have

 

  • Synthetic data, sim2real, or domain randomization experience.

  • EO / IR / LWIR, remote sensing, maritime imagery, or small-object detection experience.

  • Privacy-preserving ML, federated learning, on-prem, or air-gapped deployment experience.

  • Experience building self-serve ML platforms or tools for non-expert users.

  • Experience with lakeFS, DVC, MLflow, Weights & Biases, Kubernetes, Kubeflow, Flyte, Dagster, Airflow, or Argo.

  • LLM application, context engineering, structured output, or LLM evaluation experience.

  • Exposure to radar, AIS, EO/IR fusion, tracking, sensor fusion, robotics, autonomy, UxV, defence tech, C2/C4ISR, or tactical systems.

raw.title: Staff Software Engineer (Onboard Services)
raw.description:
UFORCE exists to make aggression unaffordable.

Founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, UFORCE is a defence-technology company with operations across Europe, the United States and Asia.

UFORCE builds uncrewed vessels, ground robotics and aircraft, autonomy software, and the command-and-control layer that operates them together. Each platform is deployable on its own, and stronger as part of the system. Its product lines include the MAGURA family of uncrewed surface vessels, the NEMESIS family of strike platforms, the LIUT family of ground robotic platforms, and counter-UAS systems.

About the role

The Staff Software Engineer (Onboard Services) will design, build, and operate the software services that run on UFORCE’s uncrewed vehicles — spanning video streaming, telemetry, autonomy integration, vehicle control, health monitoring, navigation, and device integrations.

You will turn independently evolved services into one secure, testable, and maintainable onboard platform. This is a hands-on software engineering role focused on production Python services, service architecture, messaging, and reliable operation on constrained Linux hardware, including Raspberry Pi, x86, and NVIDIA Jetson.

You will also own the boundary between the vehicle and the backend: clear, versioned contracts with cloud services, deployment systems, video infrastructure, and operator interfaces that work over intermittent, low-bandwidth links. Working with backend, autonomy, hardware, QA, and field teams, you will make releases predictable and catch failures on the bench, not in the field.

What you’ll do

  • Define and evolve a unified onboard service architecture: service boundaries, messaging, configuration, startup ordering, readiness, watchdogs, and graceful degradation when dependencies or devices are unavailable.

  • Build and migrate production services to shared patterns, using reusable libraries and a reference service template covering project structure, packaging, logging, health reporting, and lifecycle management.

  • Standardise local service communication around NATS, with clear rules for integrating MAVLink, ZMQ IPC, and HTTP where appropriate.

  • Design stable, versioned vehicle-to-backend contracts for telemetry, commands and acknowledgements, video metadata and control, configuration, health, and logs.

  • Engineer for unreliable connectivity: buffering and store-and-forward, idempotent commands, explicit acknowledgements and timeouts, reconnection, back-off, and safe behaviour when the backend is unreachable.

  • Implement secure-by-default services: least-privilege identities and messaging permissions, mutually authenticated and encrypted backend links, secure credential provisioning and rotation, sandboxed runtimes, and audit events for safety-critical commands.

  • Strengthen automated testing across unit, contract, integration, simulation, and hardware-in-the-loop tests, with CI gates that catch regressions before release.

  • Build safer release workflows with signed packages, dependency scanning, bench smoke and soak tests, staged fleet rollouts, and reliable rollback.

  • Profile services and enforce practical CPU, memory, and latency budgets on target hardware.

  • Improve field diagnostics through structured logs, metrics, standardised health reporting, post-mission log capture, and actionable runbooks.

  • Document architectural decisions and service interfaces, communicate trade-offs clearly, and use AI coding tools to accelerate delivery without compromising quality.

What success looks like

  • Actively developed onboard services converge on a shared architecture, supported Python runtime, messaging model, and service template.

  • Engineers can take a new service from an empty repository to running on a bench vehicle in a day or less, with less duplicated infrastructure code.

  • Vehicle-to-backend contracts remain compatible as cloud and vehicle software evolve at different speeds, preventing integration failures in the field.

  • Authentication, least privilege, secret handling, runtime hardening, and supply-chain checks are consistently applied across the onboard stack.

  • Automated tests and bench validation catch defects before deployment, reducing issues discovered in the field.

  • Releases move predictably from bench validation to pilot vehicles and the wider fleet, with clear readiness gates and rollback procedures.

  • Services stay within resource budgets and remain diagnosable under hardware constraints and degraded connectivity.

  • Architecture documentation and runbooks help engineering, QA, and field teams integrate changes and resolve failures faster.

Required Qualifications

  • 10+ years of professional experience in software engineering, delivering and operating production systems.

  • 2+ years as a Tech Lead or Staff Engineer, owning architecture across multiple services or teams and establishing standards adopted by others.

  • Expert Python — designs and ships production services (asyncio, packaging, testing, profiling, and performance); Node.js experience is a plus.

  • Distributed / edge system architecture — has designed service architectures and messaging systems (e.g., NATS, MQTT, ZMQ, Kafka) with versioned contracts across system boundaries and unreliable networks.

  • Web development and API experience — has built and evolved HTTP/WebSocket APIs and message-based integrations for multiple consumers.

  • Security architecture — has led the design of authentication and authorisation, secrets and key management, secure updates, and supply-chain controls; security reviews or certification evidence are a strong plus.

  • Quality engineering leadership — has established test strategies, CI gates, and staged release pipelines for a team or organisation; simulator or hardware-in-the-loop experience is a strong plus.

  • Development with AI tools — uses AI coding assistants or agents daily and has introduced practices that help a team use them effectively and safely.

  • C++, Rust, or Go experience is a plus.

  • UxV, robotics, or embedded/edge Linux experience (e.g., MAVLink, GStreamer, serial/CAN devices, systemd services on constrained hardware) is a plus.

raw.title: Advisory Data Architect
raw.description:
About Unity Advisory

Unity Advisory is a modern advisory business built for today's CFO, with connected solutions across finance, deals and tax. Focussed on client outcomes, seasoned experts lead every engagement, in an operating model powered by AI and free from audit conflict.

The Role

We are looking for an experienced Advisory Data Architect to own data design across our advisory engagements. This is a platform and design-authority role with a hands-on edge, combining finance-focused business understanding with modern data architecture, platforms and governance. You will define how data - across a client’s business - is structured, governed, and served so that AI, analytics, and management reporting are reliable and scalable. As a Senior Manager, you will lead architecture decisions, guide engineers, shape client data strategy, architecture, governance, and be accountable for the coherence and quality of the data estate you design.

This is a client-facing role within our AI Advisory team, setting the data architecture that our engagements — and our clients' AI ambitions — are built on.

Key Responsibilities

  • Define target-state data architectures for clients — models, storage, pipelines, and access patterns — balancing rigour with delivery realism.

  • Establish data modelling standards and curated domain layers across the a variety of systems (e.g. ERP, CRM, Manufacturing) and data sources, with end-to-end lineage and provenance sufficient for audit and controls.

  • Map and integrate finance source systems (ERP, EPM, sub-ledgers, and consolidation tools) into governed, analytics-ready models.

  • Design the finance data foundations for applied AI/ML: governed retrieval sources for RAG, feature stores, and the architecture that keeps AI systems fed with trustworthy, reconciled finance data.

  • Set patterns for secure, compliant finance data platforms — access control, data sensitivity, segregation of duties, isolation, and alignment to standards such as ISO 27001.

  • Provide architectural direction for cloud data platforms, infrastructure as code, CI/CD, and observability, ensuring designs are cost-aware and operable.

  • Define the data lineage and controls that support responsible production AI — monitoring, confidence scoring, and human-in-the-loop review.

  • Translate ambiguous business and client problems into clear architectural decisions and scoped roadmaps under delivery pressure.

  • Own key technical trade-offs and communicate them clearly to engineers, product stakeholders, and senior client sponsors.

  • Mentor data engineers, raise the technical bar across the team, and contribute reusable patterns, reference architectures, and accelerators.

What We're Looking For

Essential

  • Significant experience designing and delivering data architectures for production systems, with evidence that your designs have shipped and run - not remained on paper.

  • Deep expertise in data modelling, warehouse/lakehouse design, and data governance.

  • Hands-on background in SQL and Python, and fluency with at least one major cloud provider (AWS or Azure) and modern data platforms (e.g. Snowflake, Databricks).

  • System-level judgement on how data architecture shapes AI outcomes: designing governed sources for RAG, structuring data for retrieval and orchestration, and deciding where structured outputs and tool use fit.

  • Ability to set standards and lead engineers while remaining close to implementation.

  • Strong stakeholder skills, including engaging senior client sponsors and explaining architectural trade-offs clearly.

Strong Preference

  • Experience architecting the data layer behind AI or analytics products in production.

  • Informed views on the trade-offs between fine-tuning, RAG, and long-context approaches, and how each changes data architecture requirements, including context window economics and prompt caching.

  • Familiarity with infrastructure as code, CI/CD, and observability for data platforms.

  • Awareness of MCP and tool-orchestration concepts and their implications for composable, data-driven AI systems.

  • Fluent use of AI-assisted development tools (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor), with a clear view of where they help and where human design judgement must lead.

  • Security and compliance experience (e.g. ISO 27001 alignment, access control design).

  • Consulting or advisory background, owning problems end-to-end rather than a single workstream.

Nice to Have

  • Evidence of self-directed building — side projects, internal tools, or startups.

  • Exposure to finance data, PE/M&A, or portfolio-company environments.

  • Relevant certifications (e.g. AWS/Azure architect-level credentials).

raw.description:
We are Vitesse – the treasury and payment partner of choice for insurance.

Your next adventure awaits!

Join the team who are redefining the payments space.

About Us

At Vitesse, we're more than just a payments platform – we're the trusted financial infrastructure connecting the global insurance ecosystem. Tailor-made for insurers, brokers, MGAs, and TPAs, our unified platform optimises claims funds, enables real-time global payments, and delivers full financial control. Our impact is real: over $20 billion in payments across 200+ countries, hundreds of millions returned to insurers’ balance sheets, and counting. We’re licensed in the UK (FCA), Europe (DNB), and New York (NYDFS), with over 260 amazing colleagues worldwide. With $93 million recently raised in Series C funding from KKR, our journey is just beginning, and our ambitions are sky-high.

Headquartered in the heart of London and expanding across Europe and the US, Vitesse is where your ideas power tomorrow’s insurance solutions. Are you ready to make a difference? You're in the right place.

YOUR MISSION

As Senior People Partner supporting Product Engineering and Operations at Vitesse, you will operate as a strategic advisor to senior leaders, shaping and delivering a high-impact People strategy that drives performance, engagement, and scalable growth.

This role goes beyond operational HR support you will influence leadership capability, organisational design, talent strategy, and culture in a fast-moving fintech environment. You will balance commercial acumen with people expertise to ensure our teams can perform at their best while building a sustainable, inclusive and high-performing culture.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategic People Partnership

  • Partner with senior leaders to translate business objectives into actionable People strategies.

  • Act as a trusted advisor and coach to leaders, driving accountability and high performance.

Talent Strategy & Workforce Planning

  • Drive and take ownership of the workforce planning and support the Talent Acquisition team to shape hiring plans aligned to business growth and skills needs.

  • You will play an active role in supporting recruitment through coaching hiring managers to elevate hiring standards and ensure consistent, high-quality selection processes.

  • Proactively identify capability gaps and future talent risks within Product Engineering and Operations.

Performance & High-Performance Culture

  • Lead performance management cycles, ensuring robust goal setting, feedback, calibration, and development planning is in operation and meeting our standards.

  • Enable managers to confidently manage both high and low performance.

  • Embed a culture of continuous feedback, accountability, and growth.

Leadership & Capability Development

  • Diagnose development needs across teams and implement targeted learning initiatives.

  • Coach managers to strengthen leadership capability, employee engagement, and team effectiveness.

  • Support succession planning and internal mobility strategies.

Employee Relations & Risk Management

  • Serve as a trusted advisor and manager all employee relations matters within your functions and support others when and where appropriate.

  • Provide balanced, commercially sound guidance that mitigates risk while maintaining trust.

  • Ensure People practices align with employment law and regulatory requirements whilst staying in line with our people centric approach.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion

  • Embed inclusive leadership practices across Product Engineering and Operations.

  • Partner with leaders to drive equitable talent outcomes across hiring, performance, and progression.

  • Use data insights to identify and address systemic gaps.

Engagement & Culture

  • Translate engagement data into actionable insights and support with driving measurable improvements.

  • Lead retention strategies for critical talent populations.

  • Strengthen cross-functional collaboration and cultural alignment.

People Analytics & Insight

  • Leverage People data to inform decision-making and influence leadership conversations.

  • Track and report on key metrics including attrition, performance distribution, hiring effectiveness, and engagement trends.

  • Use insights to proactively identify organisational risks and opportunities.

Change & Transformation

  • Lead the People aspects of organisational change, including restructures, team evolution, and process transformation.

  • Ensure thoughtful communication, impact assessment, and change adoption strategies.

WHAT YOU NEED TO SUCCEED

  • Significant experience as a Senior HR Business Partner or Senior People Partner in a fast-paced, scaling environment ideally fintech or technology.

  • Demonstrated experience partnering with Product, Engineering, or Technical teams.

  • Strong commercial acumen and ability to link People strategy to business performance.

  • Deep understanding of employment law, regulatory frameworks, and People best practices.

  • Proven capability managing complex employee relations and organisational change.

  • A strong work ethic with high levels of ownership and accountability.

  • The confidence and credibility to operate independently, while also collaborating effectively as part of a wider People and leadership team.

  • Strong coaching and influencing skills, with the confidence to challenge senior stakeholders constructively.

  • Analytical mindset with the ability to translate People data into strategic insights.

  • A genuine passion for HR and driving our business forward as well as passion for enabling Product and Technology teams to do their best work.

We understand that everyone has their own work rhythm and believe in a flexible working schedule - at Vitesse you’re expected to work 35 hours a week.

Our Values – or what we call “Vitesse at Our Best”

The Vitesse values are a true reflection of what it takes to thrive in our business, so it’s important to us that any employee who joins our business is aligned with these 3 attributes

Confident Humility
We believe the best ideas come from listening and learning. We leave ego at the door, ask for help when we need it, and celebrate collective success. When one of us wins, we all do.

Driven to Succeed
We’re ambitious about the opportunity ahead and committed to achieving it together. We hold ourselves to high standards, take pride in what we deliver, and push for meaningful outcomes for our customers, our partners, and each other.

Tenacious Responsibility
We take ownership of our work, our decisions, and our results. We face challenges with resilience, learn from setbacks, and see things through to completion. Because doing the right thing matters.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer

We commit to creating an inclusive environment that enables everyone to perform at their best, where we recognise the rights of all individuals to mutual respect and where there is an unbiased acceptance of others. Our policies and practices aim to promote an environment that is free from all forms of unlawful or unfair discrimination and values the diversity of all people. At the heart of our policy, we seek to treat people fairly and with dignity and respect. Every agent action and asset is grounded in trust, built on an Enterprise Brain that unites brand, product, and company knowledge with fiduciary-grade governance and compliance.

As a strategic solutions architect, you'll be at the forefront of this mission, working directly with our largest and most strategic prospects to identify, validate, and build innovative generative AI solutions that unlock massive business value.   • Drive strategic technical discovery with Fortune 500 prospects and customers, translating complex business challenges into clear, impactful technical solutions for AI-powered work

  • Serve as a trusted technical advisor to C-suite executives, VPs of Engineering, and AI leaders, guiding their generative AI strategy and collaborating to define enterprise-level architecture roadmaps

  • Partner closely with WRITER's product and engineering teams, providing critical feedback from customer engagements to influence our product roadmap and ensure our solutions meet evolving market needs

  • Champion the adoption of WRITER's platform and APIs, educating prospects and partners on the art of the possible with generative AI and empowering them to build their own innovative solutions

 

⭐️ What you need

  • 5+ years of experience in technical customer-facing roles such as solutions architect, enterprise architect, or sales engineering, ideally within a high-growth, B2B SaaS company serving Fortune 500 clients

  • Experience in Python, proficiency with APIs, and end-to-end orchestration, to augment AI workflows and integrate AI capabilities into complex enterprise systems

  • Exceptional communication and presentation skills, able to simplify complex technical concepts into clear, compelling business language for diverse audiences, from technical teams to executive leadership

  • A highly versatile and tenured problem solver, capable of leading multi-stakeholder discovery sessions, uncovering root causes, and architecting innovative solutions to complex business and technical challenges

  • Comprehensive medical and dental insurance

  • Fertility and family planning support
